thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xx responses observed from us-east-2 gateway (since 3712345600). Auto-paging on-call.

maria: I’m up. seeing 502/504s for a subset of ingress pools, error rate ~6% 5xx across the region, latency + tail is up. Paging traces show increased upstream timeouts to ml-worker pool.

aj: @maria on it. Do we have recent deploys in us-east-2? I don’t see any deploys in the last 2 hours.

maria: No deploys. Checked recent rollouts: none. Grafana: request rate steady, 5xx spike correlated with higher p99 on upstream connections.

kaushik: uploading quick stack of logs — looks like connection resets from the edge proxy to mlworker-x nodes. Possibly kernel-level connection limit? Seeing many "connection reset by peer" and backlog logs.

eli: Any customers reporting errors? Support queue shows a handful of 502 tickets from EU clients routed through us-east-2 (via fallback geo routing). Not huge yet but rising.

maria: Running quick ssh to proxy nodes, tail logs:

```
# on proxy-03
2026-03-15T14:02:23Z ERROR upstream_conn.go:142 conn reset by peer: 104.16.0.5:443
2026-03-15T14:02:30Z WARN connection_pool.go:78 max_conns_reached
```

maria: Also seeing SYN cookies incrementing on a couple of hosts.

aj: Hypothesis: one of the mlworker pools is overloaded/GCing and dropping connections causing downstream gateway to return 502s. Options: (1) remove unhealthy mlworker instances from the pool, (2) divert traffic to other regions, (3) enable circuit-breaker quicker.

maria: I’m going to start draining mlworker pool us-east-2-a to stop new sessions and shift traffic to us-east-2-b and us-west-1. Applying drain now.

ops-bot: Executing drain on pool mlworker-us-east-2-a (initiated by maria). Drain command: `rctl drain pool mlworker-us-east-2-a --grace 30s`.

kaushik: I’ll watch the autoscaler and node metrics. If CPU drops and connection resets stop, likely overloaded nodes. If resets persist, maybe kernel/tcp backlog tuning.

eli: Support: putting affected customers on status page as "degraded" and telling support team to format responses: "We are seeing elevated 5xx errors in us-east-2; engineers are investigating and we've started mitigation. ETA next update: 15 minutes."

maria: Drain finished on 03, 04. Error rate dropped from 6% to 2.5% in ~60s. p95 latency still elevated.

aj: Good. Let’s also bump connection keepalive and increase proxy upstream timeout from 10s -> 15s to avoid premature 504s while we stabilize.

maria: Patching proxy config now. Command:

```
rctl config set proxy.upstream_timeout 15s --region us-east-2
rctl config set proxy.keepalive 60s --region us-east-2
```

ops-bot: Config apply in progress. Rolling restart of proxy pool with zero-downtime strategy.

kaushik: Noting that kernel netstat shows lots of TIME_WAIT and some RSTs. After draining bad workers, RST count decreased.

maria: Error rate down to 0.6% after config change + drain. Still seeing isolated 502s coming from one kube node (mlworker-us-east-2-b-7) — scheduling a cordon+restart.

aj: Go ahead. Cordon + recreate pod set on that node.

maria: `kubectl cordon mlworker-us-east-2-b-7 && kubectl drain mlworker-us-east-2-b-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — recreating pods.

eli: Support update posted. Will escalate any priority customer to on-call for real-time link.

maria: Node reboot completed. After restart, connection errors stopped. 5xx stable <0.2% for 10m.

aj: Nice. Can we re-enable the stricter timeouts? Or leave the extended upstream timeout until tomorrow morning to be safe.

maria: I suggest leaving 15s for a few hours, then roll back once autoscaler confirms headroom. Will schedule a followup.

ops-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation actions taken: drained mlworker-us-east-2-a, restarted mlworker-us-east-2-b-7, increased proxy upstream_timeout to 15s. Incident severity: SEV2 -> reevaluate in 30m.

eli: Customer impact summary for post-incident: ~2.4% of requests in us-east-2 experienced 5xx during spike window (14:00-14:07 UTC). ~12 customers reported errors, none in trial tier. No data loss.

maria: Plan: (1) keep extended timeout for 4 hours, (2) run load test on mlworker pool to reproduce, (3) investigate root cause: node-level tcp backlog + potential kernel tuning. Kaushik to own root cause. Aj to monitor for 2h; Maria will hand off in 30m.

kaushik: Will collect kernel parameters and open a follow-up ticket with exact sysctl changes tried/rolled back. Preliminary note: net.core.somaxconn maybe low on some AMIs.

aj: I'll keep watch on alerts and prepare cross-region reroute runbook if any other nodes slip.

jane: (joining) Thanks for the handoff — I’m next oncall. Any outstanding customer callbacks I should make now?

eli: Not for high-priority customers; support will alert if anything changes. We posted a status update that we're monitoring.

maria: Handoff to jane in 30s. Current status: 5xx <0.2%, mitigations completed. Followups logged in incident ticket INC-2026-3312.

jane: Acknowledged. I’ve got the runbook and will keep monitoring for 2 hours. If error rate climbs >1% again, I’ll trigger cross-region diversion to us-west-1.

incident-bot: Incident auto-closed? No — manual close required. Next status update scheduled at 3712346123.

maria: Adding final note: no deploys implicated. Likely transient node-level capacity limit. Kaushik will open postmortem and include mitigation action items: kernel tuning, improved pool health checks, and autoscaler threshold adjustments.

aj: :thumbsup: great work everyone. Short post-incident checklist: update runbooks, add check for somaxconn in bootstrap, add node-level tcp metrics to dashboard.

ops-bot: Creating follow-up ticket: TASK-2026-981: Investigate tcp backlog + autoscaler thresholds (owner: kaushik).

jane: Taking over monitoring. Handing thread to next rotation. :wave:
